name: Practice test – Comp Bible Pt 3 – Set 2 & Exam 1 Recording

slides.title: The preceptor is teaching legal principles. Which situation is an example of bat
text: Question: The preceptor is teaching legal principles. Which situation is an example of battery?
A. A nurse finds absent pulses in a casted extremity in the morning and reports it to the PHCP in the afternoon.
B. A competent client refuses an antidepressant; the nurse tells them they will be discharged if they do not take it.
C. An alert client leaves AMA; the nurse grabs the client’s arm and says they can’t leave.
D. A client on a low-sodium diet eats chips; the nurse tells the client wrist restraints will be applied.
Correct answer: C. An alert client leaves AMA; the nurse grabs the client’s arm and says they can’t leave.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Battery = unwanted physical contact. Grabbing a competent client who has the right to leave is battery (and false imprisonment). A is negligence, B is coercion, and D is assault (threat).

slides.title: The nurse should recommend an interdisciplinary conference for the pediatric cli
text: Question: The nurse should recommend an interdisciplinary conference for the pediatric client who
A. was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and has a distended abdomen.
B. is 10 hours postoperative and just urinated 30 mL of clear yellow urine.
C. is receiving hemodialysis with a potassium of 5 mEq/L.
D. has norovirus and acute diarrhea.
Correct answer: A. was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis and has a distended abdomen.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Cystic fibrosis is a chronic multisystem disease needing respiratory, nutrition, GI, and PT collaboration. A distended abdomen suggests GI obstruction/malabsorption complications. Other findings are acceptable or short-term.

slides.title: The preceptor identifies correct care when the newly hired nurse
text: Question: The preceptor identifies correct care when the newly hired nurse
A. uses sterile gloves when discontinuing a client’s IV infusion.
B. empties a client’s colostomy pouch when it is two-thirds full.
C. uses gastric pH as an indicator for correct nasogastric tube placement.
D. opens the top flap of a sterile package toward the body.
Correct answer: C. uses gastric pH as an indicator for correct nasogastric tube placement.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:

Aspirate pH ≤5 supports gastric placement (X-ray is the gold standard). Clean gloves are used to remove an IV, pouches are emptied when 1/3 full, and the outer flap of sterile packages is opened away from the body.

slides.title: A maternity nurse is floated to an adult med-surg unit. It is appropriate to ass
text: Question: A maternity nurse is floated to an adult med-surg unit. It is appropriate to assign the float nurse the client who
A. is scheduled to have an above-the-knee amputation that morning.
B. was admitted the night before with COPD.
C. is 24 hours postoperative from an appendectomy.
D. is scheduled for a cardiac catheterization after admission for chest pain.
Correct answer: C. is 24 hours postoperative from an appendectomy.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:

Assign the float nurse clients that match their skills with predictable needs. A stable postoperative client with a common surgery is the safest, and the others require specialty skills or have unstable/complex needs.

slides.title: On a pediatric cardiac unit, which client should the nurse initially assess?
text: Question: On a pediatric cardiac unit, which client should the nurse initially assess?
A. 15-year-old reading with a pulse of 60.
B. 5-year-old watching TV with a pulse of 78.
C. 2-year-old playing with toys with a pulse of 68.
D. 1-month-old sleeping with a pulse of 140.
Correct answer: C. 2-year-old playing with toys with a pulse of 68.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
A toddler’s normal HR is ~80–140, so 68 is bradycardia. The others are within normal ranges for their ages.

slides.title: A male client has a full-thickness burn to 35% of the lower body. It is a priori
text: Question: A male client has a full-thickness burn to 35% of the lower body. It is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client has a
A. pulse oximeter reading of 89%.
B. hematocrit of 60%.
C. temperature of 100.2° F.
D. urinary output of 100 mL for the past 2 hours.
Correct answer: A. pulse oximeter reading of 89%.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
SpO₂ <90–92% indicates hypoxemia (inhalation injury, carbon monoxide) — airway/breathing priority. A high Hct from fluid shifts, a low-grade fever, and 50 mL/hr output are expected.

slides.title: The nurse is prioritizing clients in a mass casualty disaster using the triage t
text: Question: The nurse is prioritizing clients in a mass casualty disaster using the triage tag system. Who should be transported first?
A. Abdominal pain and facial lacerations.
B. Burns to 75% of the posterior trunk and lower body.
C. Confused with an open wound on the right lower leg.
D. Multiple compound fractures and reports chest pain.
Correct answer: D. Multiple compound fractures and reports chest pain.
Topic: Prioritization & Delegation
notes: Rationale:
Chest pain suggests possible cardiac/pulmonary injury (fat embolus or contusion), so the client is critical but salvageable. 75% TBSA burns would be expectant in a mass casualty.

slides.title: A client with dementia is agitated and having difficulty staying in the chair. W
text: Question: A client with dementia is agitated and having difficulty staying in the chair. Which action should the nurse take first?
A. Place a seat alarm on the client’s chair.
B. Obtain a prescription to apply a vest restraint.
C. Transfer the client to bed and raise 2 side rails.
D. Place a table tray in front of the client and across their lap.
Correct answer: A. Place a seat alarm on the client’s chair.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Use the least restrictive alternative first. A seat alarm alerts staff without restricting movement; vests, trays across the lap, and raised rails are restraints.

slides.title: Which action is appropriate for the nurse to take?
text: Question: Which action is appropriate for the nurse to take?
A. Placing a client who had a stem cell transplant on contact precautions.
B. Having a client with pertussis wear an N95 during transport.
C. Initiating airborne precautions for a client with epiglottitis.
D. Wearing an N95 when caring for a client with disseminated varicella zoster.
Correct answer: D. Wearing an N95 when caring for a client with disseminated varicella zoster.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Disseminated zoster/varicella requires airborne (N95, negative pressure) plus contact precautions. Pertussis and epiglottitis are droplet, and transplant recipients need protective isolation.

slides.title: The nurse is teaching car seat safety to the parents of a 10-month-old. Which st
text: Question: The nurse is teaching car seat safety to the parents of a 10-month-old. Which statement shows correct understanding?
A. “We will place the car seat rear-facing in the middle of the back seat.”
B. “We will be sure that a hand can fit between the infant and the harness.”
C. “Our car seat is a booster seat anchored with the car lap belt.”
D. “The harness straps should be below the level of the infant’s armpits.”
Correct answer: A. “We will place the car seat rear-facing in the middle of the back seat.”
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Infants ride rear-facing in the back seat (center is safest). The harness should be snug (1–2 fingers), and rear-facing harness straps are at or below the shoulders.

slides.title: Which prescription should the nurse clarify?
text: Question: Which prescription should the nurse clarify?
A. MI 3 hours ago with a troponin level to be drawn in 3 hours.
B. Ischemic stroke symptoms for 2 hours with IV alteplase.
C. Pacemaker placed 6 months ago with a chest x-ray scheduled.
D. Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL with cardiac catheterization scheduled in the morning.
Correct answer: D. Creatinine 2.8 mg/dL with cardiac catheterization scheduled in the morning.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Contrast dye is nephrotoxic, and an elevated creatinine indicates impaired kidney function, so clarify/hydrate/hold. The other orders are appropriate (serial troponins; tPA within the window).

slides.title: Which action by the nurse is an example of PRIMARY prevention?
text: Question: Which action by the nurse is an example of PRIMARY prevention?
A. Providing a community program on stress management.
B. Instructing women how to perform monthly breast self-examination.
C. Teaching foot care to a client with diabetes and a beginning foot ulcer.
D. Referring a client who recently lost a spouse to a support group.
Correct answer: A. Providing a community program on stress management.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Primary prevention: health promotion before disease (stress management, vaccines, nutrition). BSE is secondary (screening), and foot care and support groups are tertiary.

slides.title: It is appropriate for the nurse to tell a group of men that they should
text: Question: It is appropriate for the nurse to tell a group of men that they should
A. begin annual prostate examinations at age 40.
B. begin sigmoidoscopy every 10 years at age 50.
C. perform monthly testicular self-examination immediately after a bath or shower.
D. be tested annually for STDs upon becoming sexually active.
Correct answer: C. perform monthly testicular self-examination immediately after a bath or shower.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Warm water relaxes the scrotum, making abnormalities easier to feel. Prostate screening starts at ~50 (or 40–45 if high risk), and colonoscopy is every 10 years from 45–50.

slides.title: Which statement by a newly hired nurse about infant/toddler nutrition indicates
text: Question: Which statement by a newly hired nurse about infant/toddler nutrition indicates a need for further teaching?
A. “Milk is introduced at 12 months to an infant who has been breastfed since birth.”
B. “Honey can be introduced to an infant at 9 months.”
C. “4 oz of fruit juice in a cup can be given to a 13-month-old per day.”
D. “Sliced banana is an appropriate snack for a toddler.”
Correct answer: B. “Honey can be introduced to an infant at 9 months.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Honey is avoided until after 12 months of age due to infant botulism. The other statements are acceptable.

slides.title: A client 4 hours postpartum has saturated a perineal pad in 10 minutes. What sho
text: Question: A client 4 hours postpartum has saturated a perineal pad in 10 minutes. What should the nurse do first?
A. Measure the blood pressure.
B. Assess for a distended bladder.
C. Massage the fundus.
D. Administer oxytocin.
Correct answer: C. Massage the fundus.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:

Saturating a pad in 15 minutes is postpartum hemorrhage; boggy uterine atony is the most common cause. Massage the fundus first (it is the first, non-invasive intervention), then empty the bladder, and give oxytocin per order.

slides.title: A client has right-sided paralysis after a stroke. The son says, “None of this w
text: Question: A client has right-sided paralysis after a stroke. The son says, “None of this would have happened if I had been there.” What should the nurse say?
A. “It sounds like you feel responsible for what has happened to your mother.”
B. “This must be difficult seeing your mother like this, but she will be fine.”
C. “Let’s talk about your mother’s therapy plan.”
D. “You could not have done anything to prevent this if you had been there.”
Correct answer: A. “It sounds like you feel responsible for what has happened to your mother.”
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Reflecting the son’s feelings is therapeutic. Avoid false reassurance, changing the subject, or giving a definitive statement the nurse can’t prove.

slides.title: The nurse is developing a plan of care for a client with histrionic personality
text: Question: The nurse is developing a plan of care for a client with histrionic personality disorder. Which intervention is appropriate?
A. Assist the client with appropriate behavior during group therapy sessions.
B. Work with the client on ways to develop trusting relationships.
C. Communicate with the client using casual language.
D. Utilize compassionate behavior to keep the client in control.
Correct answer: A. Assist the client with appropriate behavior during group therapy sessions.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Cluster B clients need structure, firm limits, and coaching on appropriate behavior in groups. Use direct and concrete communication, not casual or vague language.

slides.title: In the ED, a school-age child has left arm pain and several bruises on the arms
text: Question: In the ED, a school-age child has left arm pain and several bruises on the arms and legs. What should the nurse do first?
A. Separate the child from the parents until abuse is ruled out.
B. Obtain a detailed history of how the bruising occurred.
C. Report the bruising to Child Protective Services.
D. Request a psychiatric consultation.
Correct answer: B. Obtain a detailed history of how the bruising occurred.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Assess first: obtain a detailed, objective history and document. Reporting follows if suspicion remains, and avoid accusing the parents.

slides.title: The nurse is teaching the partner of a client who had a stroke and developed dys
text: Question: The nurse is teaching the partner of a client who had a stroke and developed dysphagia. Which statement indicates the need for additional teaching?
A. “Coughing while eating is a sign of dysphagia.”
B. “A change in my partner’s voice after swallowing may indicate dysphagia.”
C. “I will make sure my partner does not tilt the head forward while eating.”
D. “I should monitor for pocketing of food in the mouth.”
Correct answer: C. “I will make sure my partner does not tilt the head forward while eating.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
A chin-tuck (head forward) position closes the airway while swallowing and reduces aspiration. The other statements are correct.

slides.title: Which statement shows understanding of GERD diet and lifestyle modification?
text: Question: Which statement shows understanding of GERD diet and lifestyle modification?
A. “I will wear clothing with a spandex waistband to support my abdomen.”
B. “I will sleep with my head elevated on a wedge-style pillow.”
C. “I will sit upright for 30 minutes after meals.”
D. “I will have a snack 1 hour before bedtime.”
Correct answer: B. “I will sleep with my head elevated on a wedge-style pillow.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Elevate the head of the bed 6–8 inches (wedge pillow). Avoid tight clothing, sit upright ≥1–2 hours after meals, and avoid eating 2–3 hours before bed.

slides.title: A client died of pneumonia and an autopsy is anticipated. Which action by the ne
text: Question: A client died of pneumonia and an autopsy is anticipated. Which action by the newly hired nurse requires intervention?
A. Asking the family if they wish to participate in bathing the body.
B. Removing drainage tubes and IV lines from the body prior to autopsy.
C. Removing jewelry and placing it in a bag to return to the family.
D. Attaching 2 ID tags to the body and 1 on the outside of the shroud.
Correct answer: B. Removing drainage tubes and IV lines from the body prior to autopsy.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
When an autopsy is planned, tubes and lines are left in place. Document and secure valuables, identify the body with 3 tags, and offer family involvement.

slides.title: A client with atherosclerosis and elevated cholesterol has been taught about die
text: Question: A client with atherosclerosis and elevated cholesterol has been taught about diet. Which statement indicates a need for follow-up?
A. “I flavor my fish with lemon juice.”
B. “I cook my food with canola oil.”
C. “I take an omega-3 supplement daily.”
D. “I eat two poached eggs for breakfast every morning.”
Correct answer: D. “I eat two poached eggs for breakfast every morning.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Egg yolks are high in cholesterol (~185 mg each). Limit them, and use lean protein, fish, and unsaturated oils.

slides.title: The nurse is preparing to insert an IV catheter in an older adult. Which action
text: Question: The nurse is preparing to insert an IV catheter in an older adult. Which action is appropriate?
A. Shaving the area surrounding the vein.
B. Slapping a vein on the back of the hand.
C. Placing a washcloth between the client’s skin and the tourniquet.
D. Using a gauze dressing with paper tape.
Correct answer: C. Placing a washcloth between the client’s skin and the tourniquet.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Older adults have fragile skin and veins. Protect skin from the tourniquet, avoid slapping (hematoma), clip (not shave) hair, and use a transparent or cloth-friendly dressing/tape.

slides.title: During a PRBC transfusion the client becomes flushed and reports low back pain.
text: Question: During a PRBC transfusion the client becomes flushed and reports low back pain. After stopping the transfusion, what should the nurse do next?
A. Collect a urine specimen for the lab.
B. Notify the blood bank of a possible reaction.
C. Start 0.9% sodium chloride through new tubing.
D. Administer acetaminophen 500 mg PO.
Correct answer: C. Start 0.9% sodium chloride through new tubing.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Suspected hemolytic reaction: stop the transfusion, keep the IV open with NS via NEW tubing (to avoid infusing residual blood), then notify the provider/blood bank, check vitals, and send samples.

slides.title: A 4-year-old is to receive MMR, IPV, and DTaP. Which finding is a contraindicati
text: Question: A 4-year-old is to receive MMR, IPV, and DTaP. Which finding is a contraindication to administering the vaccines?
A. WBC of 3,900/mm³.
B. Temperature of 98.8° F.
C. Injection-site swelling and redness with previous immunizations.
D. Runny nose since yesterday.
Correct answer: A. WBC of 3,900/mm³.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Low WBC suggests possible immunosuppression — live vaccines (MMR) are contraindicated until evaluated. A mild illness, local reactions, and normal temp are not contraindications.

slides.title: A client is prescribed warfarin. Which lab value indicates a therapeutic respons
text: Question: A client is prescribed warfarin. Which lab value indicates a therapeutic response?
A. PT of 15 seconds.
B. Platelets increased from 100,000 to 150,000/mm³.
C. INR of 2.
D. aPTT increased from 30 to 60 seconds.
Correct answer: C. INR of 2.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Therapeutic INR on warfarin is 2–3. aPTT monitors heparin, and platelets are not a warfarin measure.

slides.title: Which action is appropriate when preparing an IM injection for an adult?
text: Question: Which action is appropriate when preparing an IM injection for an adult?
A. Limit the medication to 4 mL when using the deltoid muscle.
B. Hold the skin taut when using the Z-track method.
C. Use the deltoid site for a client who needs 3 mL.
D. Draw up an air bubble after the medication has been prepared.
Correct answer: B. Hold the skin taut when using the Z-track method.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Z-track: pull the skin laterally (taut) to seal the medication in the muscle. The deltoid is limited to 1 mL (ventrogluteal up to 3 mL), and the air lock is optional per policy.

slides.title: The nurse should follow up with the PHCP for a client who has
text: Question: The nurse should follow up with the PHCP for a client who has
A. constipation-predominant IBS and has been prescribed loperamide.
B. diabetes mellitus, a CT scan with IV contrast, and a prescription to withhold metformin.
C. a prosthetic mitral valve and INR 3.0 on warfarin.
D. MRSA infection, an allergy to sulfonamides, and has been prescribed vancomycin.
Correct answer: A. constipation-predominant IBS and has been prescribed loperamide.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:

Loperamide slows motility and is contraindicated in constipation. Withholding metformin around contrast is correct, INR 3 is therapeutic for mitral prosthetic valves, and vancomycin isn’t a sulfonamide.

slides.title: A client with PUD in the ED has BP 92/58 mm Hg (history of PUD, vomiting). What
text: Question: A client with PUD in the ED has BP 92/58 mm Hg (history of PUD, vomiting). What is a priority?
A. Initiate an IV nitroglycerin drip.
B. Administer an IV antiemetic.
C. Determine if the client has any stressors.
D. Type and cross for a PRBC transfusion.
Correct answer: D. Type and cross for a PRBC transfusion.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Hypotension in PUD suggests GI hemorrhage and hypovolemia, so prepare for transfusion (type and cross), start IV fluids, and notify the provider. Nitroglycerin would worsen hypotension.

slides.title: A child is postoperative from a VP shunt placement and has become difficult to a
text: Question: A child is postoperative from a VP shunt placement and has become difficult to arouse. Which action should the nurse take immediately?
A. Measure the head circumference.
B. Turn the client to the operative side.
C. Elevate the head of the bed to 30 degrees.
D. Prepare for endotracheal tube insertion.
Correct answer: C. Elevate the head of the bed to 30 degrees.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Decreased LOC suggests shunt malfunction with increased ICP. Use the least invasive intervention first (raise HOB 30°) and notify the provider. Do not lie on the shunt side.

slides.title: A client in hypovolemic shock has a pulse of 116. IV 0.9% NaCl has been initiate
text: Question: A client in hypovolemic shock has a pulse of 116. IV 0.9% NaCl has been initiated. What should the nurse do next?
A. Initiate oxygen at 2 L/min via nasal cannula.
B. Obtain a prescription for a vasodilator.
C. Document and continue to monitor.
D. Insert an indwelling urethral catheter.
Correct answer: A. Initiate oxygen at 2 L/min via nasal cannula.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Shock decreases oxygen delivery, so start oxygen, along with IV fluids. Vasodilators would worsen hypotension, and the client needs intervention, not just monitoring.

slides.title: Which ABG results should the nurse expect in a client with DKA?
text: Question: Which ABG results should the nurse expect in a client with DKA?
A. pH 7.24, PaCO₂ 50, HCO₃ 24
B. pH 7.47, PaCO₂ 38, HCO₃ 32
C. pH 7.36, PaCO₂ 42, HCO₃ 26
D. pH 7.25, PaCO₂ 35, HCO₃ 14
Correct answer: D. pH 7.25, PaCO₂ 35, HCO₃ 14
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
DKA produces metabolic acidosis: low pH and low bicarbonate, with compensatory (low-normal) CO₂ from Kussmaul breathing.

slides.title: A client with Addison disease is at risk for Addisonian crisis. Which action sho
text: Question: A client with Addison disease is at risk for Addisonian crisis. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Provide a low-carbohydrate diet.
B. Monitor blood pressure frequently.
C. Administer oral desmopressin.
D. Restrict fluid intake.
Correct answer: B. Monitor blood pressure frequently.
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Adrenal crisis causes severe hypotension, hypoglycemia, and hyponatremia. Monitor BP frequently, replace glucocorticoids/fluids, and prevent stress triggers.

slides.title: A client who had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority to notify the
text: Question: A client who had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client has
A. a fluid intake of 1,000 mL and urine output of 800 mL over 8 hours.
B. a weight increase from 199 to 201 lb over 72 hours.
C. a WBC decrease from 6,000 to 5,000/mm³.
D. a temperature increase from 99.5 to 100.3° F over 4 hours.
Correct answer: D. a temperature increase from 99.5 to 100.3° F over 4 hours.
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Immunosuppressed clients may show only subtle signs of infection or rejection; a rising temperature must be reported. Other findings are within acceptable limits.

slides.title: A client on mechanical ventilation has a high-pressure alarm. The nurse has chec
text: Question: A client on mechanical ventilation has a high-pressure alarm. The nurse has checked for potential causes and cannot determine the problem. What should the nurse do next?
A. Manually ventilate the client with a bag-mask-valve device.
B. Call respiratory therapy to check the ventilator settings.
C. Shut the alarm off and call a code.
D. Assess the client’s lung sounds and breathing pattern.
Correct answer: A. Manually ventilate the client with a bag-mask-valve device.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
If the cause cannot be found quickly, disconnect from the ventilator and manually ventilate with 100% O₂ to ensure oxygenation while help is called. The assessment was already done.

slides.title: A client is to receive a permanent pacemaker. Which statement should the nurse i
text: Question: A client is to receive a permanent pacemaker. Which statement should the nurse include in the teaching?
A. “You will need to avoid using cellular phones after the pacemaker is placed.”
B. “Swelling and redness of the operative area are normal for the first 2 days.”
C. “Avoid lifting the arm above the head on the pacemaker side for the next 4 weeks.”
D. “Keep your incision covered for the first 4 days.”
Correct answer: C. “Avoid lifting the arm above the head on the pacemaker side for the next 4 weeks.”
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Limit arm movement/raising above the shoulder until the leads are secured (about 4–6 weeks). Cell phones are fine at a distance of ~6 inches, and redness/swelling should be reported.

slides.title: Which client should be placed in a private room when admitting several clients?
text: Question: Which client should be placed in a private room when admitting several clients? (Exam 1 recording)
A. A client with inhalation anthrax diagnosed 48 hours ago.
B. A client with a fever of unknown origin.
C. A client diagnosed with HIV 2 weeks ago.
D. A client with a WBC of 2,400/mm³.
Correct answer: D. A client with a WBC of 2,400/mm³.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
A WBC of 2,400 is leukopenia/neutropenia and needs protection from infection (private/protective room). Inhalation anthrax and HIV require standard precautions only.

slides.title: Which action by the nurse is an example of SECONDARY prevention? (Exam 1 recordi
text: Question: Which action by the nurse is an example of SECONDARY prevention? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Referring a client who recently lost a spouse to a support group.
B. Performing monthly self-breast examinations.
C. Providing a community program on stress reduction.
D. Teaching foot care to a client with diabetes.
Correct answer: B. Performing monthly self-breast examinations.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Secondary prevention = early detection/screening (BSE, mammograms, labs). Stress reduction is primary, and foot care/support groups prevent progression (tertiary).

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a pregnant client whose LMP began October 21. Using Naeg
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a pregnant client whose LMP began October 21. Using Naegele’s rule, what is the due date? (Exam 1 recording — options reconstructed)
A. July 28
B. July 14
C. August 28
D. January 28
Correct answer: A. July 28
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Add 7 days: Oct 21 → Oct 28, subtract 3 months → July 28.

slides.title: A client has paranoid schizophrenia and a history of auditory hallucinations. Th
text: Question: A client has paranoid schizophrenia and a history of auditory hallucinations. The client is yelling and pacing in the dayroom, “I will do it.” What should the nurse do? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Obtain increased supervision for the client.
B. Provide the client with a diverting activity.
C. Send the client to their room.
Correct answer: A. Obtain increased supervision for the client.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
“I will do it” may be a command hallucination to harm self/others. Increase supervision for safety; you cannot divert a client actively responding to hallucinations.

slides.title: A client in the manic phase of bipolar disorder says, “I am bored.” Which activi
text: Question: A client in the manic phase of bipolar disorder says, “I am bored.” Which activity should the nurse suggest? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Walking with the nurse in the courtyard.
B. Basketball.
C. Participating in group.
Correct answer: A. Walking with the nurse in the courtyard.
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Manic clients need low-stimulation, non-competitive, solitary or one-on-one activity to burn off energy. Competitive games and groups increase stimulation.

slides.title: Which statement by a client who recently had a colostomy placed indicates a corr
text: Question: Which statement by a client who recently had a colostomy placed indicates a correct understanding of diet teaching? (Exam 1 recording)
A. “Eating yogurt can help decrease the amount of gas I have.”
B. “I should eliminate pasta from my diet so I don’t develop loose stools.”
C. “Drinking carbonated beverages can help control odor.”
D. “My largest meal of the day should be in the evening.”
Correct answer: A. “Eating yogurt can help decrease the amount of gas I have.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Yogurt/buttermilk help decrease gas and odor. Carbonated drinks increase gas, large evening meals fill the pouch overnight, and pasta is not usually restricted.

slides.title: A client who recently received hearing aids. Which statement indicates the need
text: Question: A client who recently received hearing aids. Which statement indicates the need for ADDITIONAL teaching? (Exam 1 recording)
A. “I will clean the hearing aids with alcohol wipes.”
B. “I expect the hearing aids to whistle when I cup my hand over them.”
C. “I will avoid using hair spray.”
D. “I will clean my hearing aids with soap and water.”
Correct answer: A. “I will clean the hearing aids with alcohol wipes.”
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Alcohol damages the device. Clean with a dry cloth (or a slightly damp cloth with mild soap and water — keep the device dry). Whistling when cupped is expected feedback.

slides.title: A client with asthma is prescribed beclomethasone. Which statement indicates a c
text: Question: A client with asthma is prescribed beclomethasone. Which statement indicates a correct understanding? (Exam 1 recording)
A. “I should rinse my mouth out after this medication.”
B. “I should use this medication to treat my symptoms during an asthma attack.”
C. “I need to check my pulse for 1 full minute.”
D. “I need to watch my caffeine intake.”
Correct answer: A. “I should rinse my mouth out after this medication.”
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
Beclomethasone is an inhaled corticosteroid: a controller medication, not a rescue inhaler. Rinse and spit to prevent oral thrush.

slides.title: A client is receiving IV magnesium sulfate. Which finding indicates a side effec
text: Question: A client is receiving IV magnesium sulfate. Which finding indicates a side effect? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Respiratory rate of 10/min.
B. Elevated calcium level.
C. Urinary output of 125 mL/4 hours.
D. BP change from 122/74 to 136/84.
Correct answer: A. Respiratory rate of 10/min.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:

Magnesium is a CNS depressant; toxicity causes respiratory depression, loss of deep tendon reflexes, and low urine output. The antidote is calcium gluconate. Note that 125 mL/4 hours (≈31 mL/hr) is borderline acceptable.

slides.title: A client who had an open radical prostatectomy was discharged with a urinary cat
text: Question: A client who had an open radical prostatectomy was discharged with a urinary catheter. Which statement requires follow-up? (Exam 1 recording)
A. “I will not be able to take a shower for the next 2 weeks.”
B. “I will wash my catheter once a day with soap and water.”
C. “I will change my catheter drainage bag at least once a week or as needed.”
D. “I will use a leg bag with a catheter.”
Correct answer: A. “I will not be able to take a shower for the next 2 weeks.”
Topic: Renal, Fluids & Acid-Base
notes: Rationale:
Showering is allowed with a catheter; the bag stays below the bladder. Daily soap-and-water cleaning, weekly bag changes, and leg bags are appropriate.

slides.title: The nurse is monitoring a client following a thoracentesis. It is a priority to
text: Question: The nurse is monitoring a client following a thoracentesis. It is a priority to notify the PHCP if the client develops (Exam 1 recording)
A. a heart rate increase from 95 to 110 bpm.
B. an oxygen saturation decrease from 99% to 96%.
C. vesicular breath sounds in the peripheral lung field.
D. serosanguineous drainage from the puncture site.
Correct answer: A. a heart rate increase from 95 to 110 bpm.
Topic: Respiratory
notes: Rationale:
A rising heart rate may indicate pneumothorax or bleeding/tension. Sats of 96% are normal, vesicular breath sounds are expected, and slight serosanguineous drainage is expected.

slides.title: A client in hypovolemic shock has a heart rate of 160 bpm and is receiving oxyge
text: Question: A client in hypovolemic shock has a heart rate of 160 bpm and is receiving oxygen at 2 L via nasal cannula. Which action is the priority? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Obtain a prescription to increase the oxygen to 4 L/min.
B. Document the findings and continue to monitor.
C. Notify the PHCP.
D. Administer the prescribed normal saline at 150 mL/hr.
Correct answer: D. Administer the prescribed normal saline at 150 mL/hr.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Hypovolemic shock needs volume replacement. Give the prescribed isotonic IV fluid right away, then notify the provider.

slides.title: A 3-year-old weighing 33 lb had 160 mL of urine in 8 hours. What action should t
text: Question: A 3-year-old weighing 33 lb had 160 mL of urine in 8 hours. What action should the nurse take? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Notify the PHCP.
B. Provide oral fluids.
C. Perform a bladder scan at the bedside.
D. Continue to monitor.
Correct answer: D. Continue to monitor.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
33 lb = 15 kg. 160 mL ÷ 8 hr = 20 mL/hr ≈ 1.3 mL/kg/hr, which is adequate (≥1 mL/kg/hr in children), so it is expected; keep monitoring.

slides.title: A client has developed evisceration after abdominal surgery. After calling for a
text: Question: A client has developed evisceration after abdominal surgery. After calling for assistance, which action should the nurse take next? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Place the client in a supine position with the knees drawn toward the abdomen.
B. Use a moist ABD pad to cover the abdomen.
Correct answer: B. Use a moist ABD pad to cover the abdomen.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:

Evisceration: call for help, cover the viscera with a sterile saline-moistened dressing (keeps the organs from drying), position low Fowler’s with knees bent to reduce abdominal tension, and notify the surgeon.

slides.title: The PACU nurse assesses a client who had a below-the-knee amputation. What shoul
text: Question: The PACU nurse assesses a client who had a below-the-knee amputation. What should the nurse prioritize assessing for? (Exam 1 recording)
A. Hypovolemic shock from bleeding.
B. Neurogenic shock.
Correct answer: A. Hypovolemic shock from bleeding.
Topic: Burns, Trauma & Emergencies
notes: Rationale:
Major bleeding is the earliest, most life-threatening complication after amputation, so check the residual limb dressing and vital signs; keep a tourniquet at the bedside.

slides.title: A client had lumbar spinal surgery 8 hours ago. It is a priority to notify the s
text: Question: A client had lumbar spinal surgery 8 hours ago. It is a priority to notify the surgeon if the client (Exam 1 recording)
A. independently log-rolls in bed.
B. has 125 mL serosanguineous fluid in the Hemovac.
C. has a moderate amount of clear drainage on the surgical dressing.
Correct answer: C. has a moderate amount of clear drainage on the surgical dressing.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Clear (halo-ring/glucose-positive) drainage suggests a cerebrospinal fluid leak, which risks meningitis and requires immediate reporting. Log-rolling and serosanguineous drainage are expected.

slides.title: A client is on bed rest. Which action will help prevent pulmonary embolism? (Exa
text: Question: A client is on bed rest. Which action will help prevent pulmonary embolism? (Exam 1 recording — one option missing in source)
A. Determine if the client is using the incentive spirometer.
B. Instruct the client to perform leg exercises.
C. Elevate the client’s legs on a pillow.
Correct answer: B. Instruct the client to perform leg exercises.
Topic: Cardiovascular
notes: Rationale:
Leg exercises/ROM prevent venous stasis and DVT (a PE source). Incentive spirometry prevents atelectasis/pneumonia, and pillows under the knees can impair venous return.

slides.title: Which sequence correctly describes removal (doffing) of personal protective equi
text: Question: Which sequence correctly describes removal (doffing) of personal protective equipment? (Exam 1 recording — options reconstructed)
A. Gloves, goggles, gown, mask
B. Mask, gown, goggles, gloves
C. Gown, gloves, mask, goggles
D. Goggles, mask, gloves, gown
Correct answer: A. Gloves, goggles, gown, mask
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Remove the most contaminated items first: gloves → goggles/face shield → gown → mask (mask last, outside the room), followed by hand hygiene.
